speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: The package has $290 million dollars in direct support to dairy farmers, but most importantly, it means some hope for them. One of the things Senator Sanders and I, Congressman Welch, realized as we went around the state, dairy farmers are hurting and hurting terribly. They need some hope, as it is now. Every day they stay in Daring is a day that they lose money.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: We want to get them back where they're profitable. They're a major part of our community, major part of our state, major part of every town and village they're in. We want to get them back on their feet. Fortunately, we have a Secretary of Agriculture who understands this. We've met with Secretary Vilsack. I've talked to him on the phone, talked to him in meetings in my office. He understands the need. He's not going to hold this

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: This administration has been very, very supportive of us. The Obama administration very supportive of dairy farms. I think that's good news right there because there's a lot of flexibility for the secretary. I think he's going to be using that flexibility plus the money that the Sanders, Leahy et al. amendment gives him.

speaker: SPEAKER_00
text: Well, the Vermont delegation has shown they can put together bipartisan coalitions, national coalitions, to help on these, and we've had the experience, we have the contacts, we do it. We get Republicans and Democrats together behind the legislation. In the meantime, I've also been meeting with leaders of the dairy industry from across the country, and they're going to have to take some new steps, too, but in the short term, we will help with the money.
